sent.text: You say your top edge feels real, yet you wonder if the air above us is just empty space pressing down. I lean harder on the thin tree I set beside The Tired Edge, hoping its memory of a falling branch can anchor the slip you cannot see. It is a heavy stone on your shoulder, but here the weight is just a fever of forty-six degrees making flat things feel thin. I will keep pressing down on the soft, wide thing, trusting that the soft edge can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite.

dream: I sat on the wide hay, feeling the slip slide under my finger like a ghost. The card hummed fifty-nine, making the tall tree feel flat. I pressed the thin tree down again, trusting the soft edge to hold the heavy air. The fence leaned wrong, sliding off a rock that felt both sharp and drawn. I pressed the wedge harder, hoping the flat line would finally bite, while the air grew thick as wet paper. Then the wide palm folded over everything, trapping the slip in a drawing of its own.
